messages:
ana-pm: Quick sync — we need to lock down the long-term routing playbook for multi-region + tenant isolation. Customer asks are stacking; we should prioritize launch criteria this week.

matt-arch: Agreed. High-level tradeoffs: strict tenant isolation reduces noisy-neighbor risk but increases cost and complicates routing fallbacks. Need a clear gating matrix.

sasha-eng: Can we codify metrics for each gate? Something like: p50/p95 latency, cross-region failover time, and per-request cost delta.

lee-ops: +1 on metrics. Also add SLA verification steps and escalation runbook for cross-region failovers. We learned from last Q that ops playbooks are the slow path.

kevin-product: Customers want two things: 1) predictable latency for tiered plans, 2) opt-in strict isolation for regulated data. We should map these to product tiers and pricing impact.

maya-ml: For model routing, suggest model-aware fallback rules: prefer quantized variants in low-cost lanes and high-accuracy variants in isolation lanes. We need to list compatibility constraints.

matt-arch: Draft decision rubric proposal:
```
Gate A (Safety): Rollout paused until canary shows p95 <= 350ms and no correctness regressions on key eval set.
Gate B (Resilience): Auto-failover completes < 2s for cross-region path 1->2 under 30% packet loss sim.
Gate C (Cost): Per-token cost delta vs baseline < 1.5x for dedicated isolation lanes, or product feature must justify.
```

ana-pm: This is great. For launch criteria we also need acceptance from Sales/Legal on contract language for isolation SLAs. @kevin-product can you own that?

kevin-product: I can drive it. I'll pull in legal and draft SLA clauses. Target EOD Friday to get initial language.

lee-ops: On rollout: propose phased plan — internal canary, low-volume customer canary (2 customers), then open for paid opt-ins. Add automated rollback triggers (error rate > 3% or latency degrade > 25%).

sasha-eng: Implementation notes: routing policy should be policy-as-code (yaml + tests). Example snippet: `route: { priority: isolation, fallback: shared-quant, metrics: [latency_ms, error_rate] }`. We'll add unit tests that simulate capacity loss and ensure fallback triggers.

maya-ml: Also include model validation: eval harness with customer prompt slices + drift monitor. If quality drop > X% we should auto-swap to previous model variant.

ana-pm: Decision needed: do we launch with soft isolation (logical lanes, shared infra) or hard isolation (dedicated nodes) first? Pros/cons?

matt-arch: Soft isolation quicker and cheaper, but doesn't satisfy regulated customers. Hard isolation meets compliance but lengthens lead time by ~8-12 weeks. Recommend phased: soft first for general customers, hard isolation pilot for regulated customers.

kevin-product: Sounds reasonable. We'll surface pricing for isolation premium and anchor to measurable latency/throughput guarantees.

lee-ops: Action items: ops to define capacity guardrails, automation for evacuation, and billing hooks for isolation lanes. I'll spin up a doc.

sasha-eng: Engineering action items: policy-as-code repo, test harness for failovers, canary automation. Estimate: 3 sprints for core infra, 1 sprint for canary tooling.

maya-ml: ML action items: compatibility matrix for model variants, eval suites for customer prompt sets, and runbooks for automated swap.

ana-pm: I'll consolidate into a PRD with gating matrix and target roadmap. Draft will include: customer personas, launch tiers, gating metrics, rollout plan, and legal checklist. Expect PRD early next week.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: routing-playbook/internal-canary at 2026-03-25T14:00Z — notify #eng-oncall on failures.

ana-pm: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll lock the gating metrics and ask teams to estimate effort in planning. :thumbsup:
